name: Samgar-nebu
overview: Samgar-nebu was a male Babylonian official who held a position of authority by sitting in the Middle Gate of Jerusalem. The Bible specifically mentions him in the context of Jerusalem during the Babylonian period, indicating his role in the city's administration under Babylonian rule.
namesAndTitles: The only recorded name for this individual is Samgar-nebu, with no meaning or special significance provided in the biblical text. Therefore, his name is simply acknowledged as a proper name without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Samgar-nebu beyond his official capacity described in the text. No relatives or personal connections are mentioned.
scriptureSignificance: Samgar-nebu's significance lies in his role as a Babylonian official stationed at a key location in Jerusalem, the Middle Gate. His presence serves as a historical marker of the Babylonian occupation and administrative structure within the city.
